liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Franklin's Tower** (2 reviews): Reviewer finds the vocals too passive, with forgotten words; Reviewer says Jerry fumbled the lyrics and sang a verse out of order; Bob tried to rescue it [14][19]
- **Stella Blue** (1 review): Reviewer singles out Stella Blue as an excellent version and the part of the show they recall [10]
- **Jack Straw** (1 review): Reviewer calls Jack Straw an outstanding version [11]
- **Feel Like A Stranger** (1 review): Rhythm is solid but the performance lacks fire, per the reviewer [14]

## Setlist highlights

- **gd88-10-21 t01 Crowd**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [20]
- **gd88-10-21 t02 Let The Good Times Roll**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [20]
- **gd88-10-21 t03 Feel Like A Stranger**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [20]
- **gd88-10-21 t04 Franklin's Tower**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [20]
- **gd88-10-21 t05 Walkin' Blues**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [20]
- **gd88-10-21 t06 Believe It Or Not**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [20]
- **gd88-10-21 t07 Memphis Blues Again**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [20]
- **gd88-10-21 t08 Dupree's Diamond Blues**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [20]

## The recordings

- **gd1988-10-21.141657.schoeps.cmc3.mk41.pcm.mattes.miller.clugston.flac1644** (recommended): audience recording; 23 songs; 150 min [1]
- **gd88-10-21.dsbd.miller.30814.sbeok.flacf**: soundboard; 21 songs; 144 min; rated 3.88/5 by 17 [2]. Said about its sound: Good sound with solid dynamics, but heavy hiss on the first three songs [11]
- **gd88-10-21.sbd.dodd.16188.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 21 songs; 135 min; rated 4.5/5 by 2 [4]. Said about its sound: Reviewer says this soundboard is far better in quality than another copy of the show they own [8]
- **gd88-10-21.aud.ford-bryson.31108.sbeok.flacf**: audience recording; 21 songs; 137 min; rated 3.25/5 by 4 [5]. Said about its sound: Set I is recorded too high, with distortion especially on disc one tracks three and four [5]

## Around the show

- Reviewer attended this show, the only Dead concert they ever saw, and remembers little of it [10]
- Reviewer had followed the band for 15 years; this was their last Dead show [12]
- Reviewer's last show closed with Sugar Magnolia and the Brokedown Palace encore [12]
- Reviewer describes this as the final night of the Fall '88 tour [14]
- Reviewer drove from Austin; the Dallas weather was sunny, about 70 degrees, with no humidity [18]
- Reviewer recalls Brent being drunk on his birthday and falling off his piano bench [18]
- Happy Birthday was sung for Brent's 36th before Wang Dang Doodle [1]
- Reviewer says late-80s shows don't match mid-to-late 70s ones, but this has good jams [8]
- Reviewer calls it a very nice show from a high point in the band's career [19]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1988-10-21.141657.schoeps.cmc3.mk41.pcm.mattes.miller.clugston.flac1644**: taped by Ted Mattes; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Source Info: Ted Mattes' Master Audience PCM (OTS); Schoeps CMC3/MK41 > Oade P/S > Sony PCM-F1 > Sony SL-2000; Transfer Info: PCM (Sony SL-10)> Sony PCM-601ESD… [1]
- **gd88-10-21.dsbd.miller.30814.sbeok.flacf**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Dat [2]. Also: Reviewer taped the radio broadcast of this show and replayed it many times [15]
- **gd88-10-21.sbd.dodd.16188.sbeok.shnf**: source: MSC>?>DAT>CDR Eac > cool edit > shntool > cdwav > shnv3 Dat> Cdr by Andy Lemieux Eac > shnv3(secure with proper offsets) by Ernie Dodd [4]
- **gd88-10-21.aud.ford-bryson.31108.sbeok.flacf**: transferred by Alex Ford; source: Audience: Nakamichi mics [5]. Also: This audience recording comes from first-generation cassettes supplied by Barry B; First-generation cassettes were recorded with Dolby B; this transfer was made with Dolby off on playback [5][16]
